notes.wakayima: The trickster hero of East African folktales.

guidebook.intro: The last unit of the course goes back to the fireside: trickster tales that every Swahili-speaking child knows, and the lessons tucked inside them.

tips.title: Him, her, us: object markers
body: The person an action is done to goes inside the verb, right before the root: **-ni-** (me), **-ku-** (you), **-m-** (him or her), **-tu-** (us), **-wa-** (them).
**alimdanganya** = a-li-**m**-danganya (he tricked him), **inatufundisha** = i-na-**tu**-fundisha (it teaches us). You’ve used this since **Nakupenda** (I love you).

culture.title: Sungura and Abunuwasi
body: **Sungura** the hare is small but always outwits the bigger animals, especially the greedy **fisi** (hyena).
**Abunuwasi** grew out of Abu Nuwas, a poet of old Baghdad, who travelled into Swahili tales as a trickster who makes fools of kings and judges.
